status: evidence-backed research opportunity; novelty not established
claim: Published work evaluates query-plan novelty, SQL validity feedback, and historical clause/call-chain targeting under materially different databases, budgets, oracles, and deduplication/confirmation rules. Thus published headline bug counts do not support ranking these guidance signals, and the cross-method calibration of proxy signals against vendor-confirmed, root-cause-distinct logic bugs remains an actionable empirical question.

sources.title: SQLaser: Detecting DBMS Logic Bugs with Clause-Guided Fuzzing
locators: §3: 144 historical bugs analyzed into 35 clause patterns
§6.1: 22 bug instances, 4 vendor-confirmed distinct-root-cause new bugs; oracle incompleteness caveat
§6.2.1: SQLite comparison includes 60-day runs; reports approximately 60% lower detection time

interpretation: The three guidance mechanisms plausibly target complementary bottlenecks (valid input generation, state/plan diversity, and known error-prone interactions), but this synthesis is a hypothesis. The primary finding is an empirical comparison/calibration gap; it does not establish a novel integrated method.
falsifiable_question: Under matched DBMS versions, test oracles, CPU-hour budgets, hardware, seed policy, and blinded vendor-confirmed root-cause deduplication, do validity feedback, query-plan novelty, and historical clause/call-chain targeting each increase confirmed unique logic-bug yield, and are their effects complementary?
primary_outcome: Vendor-confirmed root-cause-distinct logic bugs per CPU-hour; time to first confirmed unique logic bug.
counterevidence_and_caveats: QPG already includes repeated multi-DBMS evaluations and sensitivity analysis; the gap is cross-method matched comparison, not lack of QPG validation.
SQLancer++ already performs a single-system feedback ablation, so novelty must focus on cross-system calibration, interactions, and uniform outcome adjudication.
SQLaser reports a 60-day evaluation and identifies missing-oracle coverage as a limitation.
This was a targeted full-text audit of three primary papers, not a systematic literature review or independent replication.
Novelty is unconfirmed.
suggested_design: Run a preregistered factorial ablation, first 2x2 validity-feedback by plan-novelty on SQLite, then add clause/call-chain targeting and expand to at least four open-source DBMSs. Pin commits and oracles; equalize CPU time; use at least 10 seeds; blind root-cause triage and report per-system outcomes and uncertainty.

status: replicated cross-study evaluation insight; candidate moderator question
claim: Fuzzer rankings change with outcome metric: in a 9-fuzzer, 12-system FuzzBench study FairFuzz ranked poorly on bug-finding efficacy but strongly on selected time-efficiency metrics, while coverage-to-bug correlation varied more by software-under-test than by fuzzer. Therefore coverage or aggregate bug counts alone can mis-rank practical utility.

locators: Abstract and §§4–5: coverage gains differ by benchmark; results are target-dependent

sources.title: Comparing Fuzzers on a Level Playing Field with FuzzBench
locators: Abstract, PDF p.1: efficacy/efficiency distinction and SUT-dependent coverage-bug correlation
§III, PDF pp.3–4: 9 fuzzers, 12 systems, 30 runs per pair, 23 hours per run
§V and §VII: FairFuzz metric-dependent ranking

interpretation: This is a direct empirical result for crash-oriented general-purpose fuzzing under the study's targets and metric definitions; deduplicated crashes are only proxies for confirmed distinct root causes, and the result does not make FairFuzz universally superior.
falsifiable_question: Across preregistered target classes, do program features, seed quality, and sanitizer configuration moderate the effect of rare-branch guidance on confirmed unique bugs per CPU-hour, independently of coverage?
primary_outcome: Confirmed distinct root-cause bugs per CPU-hour, with known-bug recall and time-to-first-bug reported separately.
counterevidence_and_caveats: FuzzBench itself used a reproducible 30-run, 23-hour design and ground-truth bugs, so this is stronger than an anecdotal metric conflict.
Crash deduplication can still over- or under-merge underlying bugs.
Target programs and fuzzers are a finite 2022-era sample; modern targets may differ.
suggested_design: Re-run rare-branch and baseline fuzzers on contemporary target families with pinned versions, 30 seeds, equal CPU-hour budgets, sanitizer strata, and blinded root-cause adjudication; model target-by-method interactions.

status: cross-paper methodological reconciliation; transfer question open
claim: For code-generation correctness, uncertainty estimates in the audited studies are sensitive to how semantically equivalent programs are clustered. Natural-language/code-embedding and CodeBLEU clustering were weak in the 2025 LiveCodeBench study, while bounded symbolic-execution clustering recovered correlation and enabled low-false-positive abstention; this provides a plausible methodological explanation for heterogeneous earlier results, but does not establish repository-level generalization.

sources.title: Assessing Correctness in LLM-Based Code Generation via Uncertainty Estimation
locators: §4 and Table 2: clustering-specific correlation results
§5 / Table 3: abstention false-positive/false-negative outcomes
Limitations: 10-second symbolic equivalence timeout and loop unrolling

interpretation: The later paper is constructive counterevidence to a blanket claim that uncertainty fails for code: the signal worked under a more precise equivalence proxy. Its bounded checker can falsely merge non-equivalent programs, and its tested models/tasks are limited.
falsifiable_question: On repository-level code repair and code translation, does symbolic equivalence improve uncertainty calibration and selective risk enough to justify execution cost and bounded-checker error, across project sizes and unseen repositories?
primary_outcome: Risk-coverage curves and calibration for human-verified correctness, including false acceptance, unnecessary abstention, checker timeout, and compute cost.
counterevidence_and_caveats: The 2025 study reports useful results for symbolic clustering, not just a future-work claim.
Symbolic execution is bounded and may falsely infer equivalence when a distinguishing behavior lies beyond loop-unrolling or timeout bounds.
Only a limited set of NLG uncertainty methods and code benchmarks were tested; newer estimators may change the comparison.
suggested_design: Use repository-held-out repair/translation sets, matched model samples, independent human or test-suite labels, and a timeout-aware symbolic-equivalence checker; compare semantic entropy, code embedding, CodeBLEU, and log-probability at equal inference-plus-checker cost.

status: multi-environment source result; moderator hypothesis needs independent replication
claim: In MemGym's paired same-reasoner experiments, summary memory was approximately neutral or harmful on coding tasks where progress could be re-read from the filesystem, while memory improved success on dialogue and web tasks with state hidden in prior turns or absent from the current DOM. This suggests recoverability of task state may moderate the net value of explicit agent memory.

sources.title: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
locators: §4.1: paired evaluations, models, task sizes, and common compaction trigger
§4.2, Table 2: SWE-Gym memory deltas of 0/-1.0/-3.2 pp vs dialogue +8.7 pp and WebArena +4.3 pp
§4.2: state recoverability interpretation
§4.4 / Appendix J: OOD scope and limitations

interpretation: The result is a within-paper cross-environment comparison, not a universal law. Strategy/model/domain confounds are reduced by fixed-reasoner paired runs but not eliminated; one benchmark paper cannot establish an independently replicated moderator mechanism.
falsifiable_question: Does the ability to recover state from files, logs, DOM, or external knowledge predict the causal benefit of explicit memory when context pressure, model, memory strategy, and token/API cost are controlled?
primary_outcome: Paired task-success delta and total cost (tokens, rereads, retrieval calls) under explicit memory vs no-memory controls.
counterevidence_and_caveats: Coding tasks were tested on SWE-Gym and may not represent other coding environments or memory mechanisms.
The observed memory benefit differs by task and model; this is moderator evidence, not proof of a single cause.
MemGym's synthetic memory tasks deliberately force memory dependence and do not establish field deployment benefits.
suggested_design: Randomize external state recoverability and context pressure in coding, dialogue, and browser tasks; use paired seeds and fixed reasoners, compare memory strategies and no-memory baselines, and account for all inference/retrieval costs.

status: cross-regime conditional finding; matched replication needed
claim: Sparse static communication topologies have shown token savings with comparable or better performance on selected debate/reasoning and labeling tasks, while a long-horizon collaboration benchmark reports that a fixed shared plan without communication underperformed its no-communication baseline. These are not direct contradictions; together they indicate that communication topology effects may depend on whether the task state and plan must be revised dynamically.

locators: §4, Tables 1/3–5: sparse connectivity, accuracy, token-cost results
§9 Limitations: static graphs, restricted models/tasks, no optimal topology rule

sources.title: AgentWorld: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Collaboration of Multi-agent LLMs
locators: §4.4, Table 3: shared-plan/no-communication 17.6%, no-communication 22.9%, vanilla multi-agent 52.0%
§4.4: baseline definitions and communication/plan interpretation
§4: model and task evaluation scope

interpretation: The papers use different tasks and systems. The shared-plan result does not test sparse communication directly, so the defensible synthesis is a transfer hypothesis about static versus dynamic coordination, not evidence that sparse topologies fail in long-horizon tasks.
falsifiable_question: At equal token/API budgets, does an adaptive communication topology preserve sparse-debate cost savings while improving long-horizon tasks that require plan revision, compared with fixed sparse, fully connected, and shared-plan/no-communication controls?
primary_outcome: Task success per fixed token/API budget, with plan revision quality, useful-message rate, and latency as secondary outcomes.
counterevidence_and_caveats: Sparse debate study reports positive results across multiple selected task types, so the hypothesis must preserve the possibility that sparse communication remains effective.
AgentWorld's shared-plan baseline is not an ablation of communication graph sparsity and is not directly comparable to the debate paper.
Both papers have different models, evaluation harnesses, and cost definitions.
suggested_design: Create matched static-answer and dynamic-coordination tasks; sweep fixed sparse/dense/adaptive graphs at equal token/API budgets, freeze model and prompts, randomize seeds, and measure plan-change events and communication utility.

topic: automated program repair; dataset contamination and robustness
status: independent cross-study evidence; magnitude and mechanism not resolved
claim: Semantics-preserving code transformations reduce repair performance in multiple APR studies, but the magnitude and likely mechanism vary by benchmark age, model set, transformation protocol, and success metric. A 2025 Defects4J-Trans study reports mean correct/plausible patch-count drops of 49.48%/42.90%; an independent 2026 study reports Defects4J per-model success-rate drops of about 4.01–15.98 percentage points, while two closed models show no significant average decline on the newer GitBug-Java set. In the 2026 study, transformation drops among open models associate with low-NLL familiarity in part of the distribution, but high-NLL cases also show brittleness.

locators: Abstract: 11-model average decreases in correct and plausible patch counts
§III-D: 200 invocations per bug; plausible versus correct patch definitions
§IV-A, Table II: model-specific Defects4J to Defects4J-Trans changes

sources.title: A Metamorphic Testing Approach to Diagnosing Memorization in LLM-Based Program Repair
locators: §III: two benchmark datasets, transformations, prompts, ten repetitions and test-adequacy outcome
§IV-A, Table II: model/dataset transformed success-rate changes and significance
§IV-B: NLL associations and inverted-U brittleness pattern
§VI Threats to Validity: test-adequate patches are not necessarily semantically correct

interpretation: Both papers support transformation sensitivity, but their headline effect sizes are not directly comparable: model populations, transformed benchmarks, repetition/patch protocols, and denominators differ. The newer paper gives convergent evidence linking some drops to NLL-based familiarity, not definitive causal proof of training-set leakage; transformation sensitivity also appears among unfamiliar examples.
falsifiable_question: Under a single preregistered APR protocol, how much of transformation-induced repair loss is attributable to benchmark familiarity versus general syntactic/semantic brittleness, and does combining natural metamorphic deltas with model-accessible NLL improve contamination diagnosis over either alone?
primary_outcome: Human-verified correct repair rate and plausible-patch rate on original and transformed versions, with paired bug-level effects; secondary outcomes include NLL, transformation type, model access, and benchmark age.
counterevidence_and_caveats: 2026 study reports no statistically significant mean decline for Claude-3.7/GPT-4o on GitBug-Java; smaller solvable-bug sample limits power.
2026 paper uses test-adequate patches at scale; passing tests does not prove semantic correctness.
2025 and 2026 estimates use different models, transformations, datasets, repetitions, and outcome denominators; do not interpret them as a direct numerical contradiction.
NLL is unavailable for proprietary models and is only a proxy for familiarity; metamorphic drop is not by itself proof of leakage.
suggested_design: Use the same recent and historic Java bugs, verified natural semantics-preserving transformations, matched models and sampling budgets, multiple candidate patch counts fixed in advance, and blinded human correctness labels. Measure paired effects by dataset vintage and transformation class; test preregistered interactions with NLL where model weights permit.
